item.name: Read me first
item.description:
Docs version 1.1.0 (2026-11-21)

# Tayari API v1

One API for three apps: the **Flutter app** (customers and business owners on mobile), the **React website** (customers and businesses on the web) and the **React admin panel** (Tayari staff). Every endpoint in this collection sits in the folder of the app that uses it, next to the screen that calls it.

## Base URL and versions

- All endpoints start with `{{baseUrl}}` = `{{appUrl}}/api/v1` (for example `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`).
- `v1` stays stable. A breaking change gets a new version (`/api/v2`); old apps keep working on `v1` until they update.
- **426 Upgrade Required** means this mobile app version is too old: show the force-update screen and send the user to the store. It only happens on Android and iOS, never on the web.

## Headers on every request

- `Accept: application/json`: always send it, so every answer is JSON.
- `Accept-Language: ar` or `en`: the language of every message and of translated names (for example business types). Anything else, or no header, means Arabic.
- `X-Platform: android`, `ios` or `web`: which app is calling.
- `X-App-Version` (mobile only, for example `1.4.0`): the installed app version. The server compares it with the minimum version and answers **426** when it is lower.

This collection adds these headers for you (see the scripts on the app folders).

## How each app logs in

- **Flutter app:** `POST auth/token` returns a **Bearer token**. Store it securely and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. Logout deletes it on the server.
- **React website and admin panel:** a **session cookie** (Laravel Sanctum). First call `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`, then `POST auth/login`. Send every request with cookies (`credentials: 'include'` in fetch, `withCredentials: true` in axios) and the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header taken from the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie (axios does this by itself). The website must run on a domain the server trusts (`SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS`).
- **Postman setup for the React folders:** open **Cookies › Domains Allowlist** and add the host of `{{appUrl}}` (for example `localhost`). Otherwise the folder script can't read the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and requests answer **419**. The Postman console shows a warning when this is missing.

## Errors

Every error has the same shape:

```json
{
  "message": "A short message for the user, in the request language.",
  "errors": { "phone": ["The phone number field is required."] }
}
```

- Show each `errors.<field>` message under its input.
- Show `message` in a toast, snackbar or dialog. `errors` is an empty object when there are no field errors.

## Status codes every app must handle

- **200, 201, 204:** success (201 = created, 204 = success with no body).
- **401:** not logged in, or the token or session expired. Clear the stored login and go to the Login screen.
- **403:** the account is blocked, the phone is not verified, or the user isn't allowed to do this. Show `message` as it is.
- **404:** not found. Show a "not found" state.
- **419 (web only):** the CSRF cookie is missing or old. Call `sanctum/csrf-cookie` again and retry once.
- **422:** invalid input. Show `errors` under the fields.
- **426 (mobile only):** force update.
- **429:** too many attempts. Most limits are per phone number and per IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit); login counts tries per phone number from the same IP address, plus an hourly limit per phone number. Wait (see the `Retry-After` header, in seconds) and let the user retry.
- **500:** something went wrong on the server. Show a generic error and let the user retry.

## Lists and pages

Lists are paginated. Send `page` (starts at 1) and `per_page` (default 20, at most 100). The answer has:

- `data`: the items of this page;
- `meta`: `current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `from`, `to`;
- `links`: `first`, `last`, `prev` and `next` URLs (`next` is null on the last page).

## Language, dates and documents

- Messages and translated names follow `Accept-Language`. The language at sign up is saved on the account and used for SMS.
- All dates are UTC in ISO 8601 (for example `2026-11-21T09:30:00Z`). Convert them to the user's time zone before showing them.
- Personal and business documents are private. API responses include a short signed `url` for each file, valid for 5 minutes. Open it as it is; when it expires, load the screen data again to get a new URL.
- Phone numbers can be typed in any Egyptian mobile format (`010…`, `+2010…`, Arabic digits). The server saves and returns them as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.

## Endpoints no app calls directly

- `GET /api/v1/media/{media}`: Private documents are only opened through the short signed `url` the API returns (for example in `auth/me` or a business profile). Use that URL as it is, in an image view, a PDF viewer or a new tab; never build it yourself.

item.name: Changelog
item.description:
## 1.1.0 (2026-11-21)

- Admin panel, Business types: list active and inactive types with search, show, create, update, activate, deactivate, and delete (only when no business profile uses the type; otherwise a 422 asks to deactivate it instead). Names must be unique in each language, ignoring letter case.
- Admin panel, Users: list customer and business accounts with search by name, full phone or part of a phone, and filters (account type, status, phone verified, national ID status, business profile status); user details with the national ID and the business profile; block with a reason and unblock.
- Admin panel, Staff (super admins only): list staff, create a staff member (admin, ops or support), change a role, block and unblock. Nobody can change their own role or block themselves, and the last active super admin can't be blocked or demoted.
- Admin panel, Business profiles review: the Review details page now uses the new **Get business profile** endpoint, which also returns `reviewed_by`.
- New permissions: `business_types.view`, `business_types.manage`, `users.view`, `users.block` and `staff.manage`. Admin has every permission except `staff.manage`; ops gets the business types and users view permissions and `users.block`; support gets the business types and users view permissions.
- Login rate limits, clearer wording: tries are counted per phone number from the same IP address, plus an hourly limit per phone number from any IP address.
- Example bodies: the `reason` example in the reject and block requests is now a neutral placeholder.

## 1.0.0 (2026-11-21)

- App config and force update: minimum and latest app versions per platform, the phone verification switch and the server time; old mobile apps get 426 and must update.
- Sign up, with the phone verification switch: when it is on, an SMS code (OTP) is sent, then Verify phone and Resend code.
- Login: a Bearer token for the Flutter app, a session cookie for the React website and admin panel.
- Forgot password and Reset password with an SMS code.
- Account: Get my account, Change password and Log out.
- Push tokens: save and remove the FCM token of a device (Flutter app).
- Business types for the business type picker.
- Business profile and documents: create, show and update the profile, and upload the national ID sides, the commercial register and the tax card.
- Optional national ID upload for any customer.
- Admin review of business profiles and national IDs: list, approve or verify, and reject with a reason.
- Roles and permissions for the admin menu: `roles` and `permissions` are always returned (empty for customers), a super admin gets every permission, and the menu and buttons are built from `permissions` only.
- Postman setup for the cookie flow: allowlist the host of `{{appUrl}}` under Cookies › Domains Allowlist, then call Get CSRF cookie before Log in.
- Rate limits per phone number and per IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit).

item.name: Flutter app
item.description:
The mobile app for customers and business owners (Android and iOS).

- **Login:** Bearer token from **Sign up and login › Log in**. Its script saves the token to `{{token}}`, and every request in this folder sends it.
- **Headers:** this folder adds `X-Platform: {{platform}}` (`android` by default; set `ios` in the environment) and `X-App-Version: {{appVersion}}`.
- Build the folders in order: app start, sign up and login, account, push notifications, then the business and national ID screens.

item.name: 1. App start
item.description:
What the app does on the **Splash** screen, before anything else:

1. Call **Get app config**.
2. If the installed version is lower than `min_supported_version` for this platform, show the **force-update** screen (no way past it) with a button to the store.
3. Else, if it is lower than `latest_version`, show an **optional update** dialog ("Update" / "Later").
4. Keep `phone_verification_required`: it decides whether the OTP screen comes after sign up.
5. If a token is stored, go to Home (and call **Get my account**); otherwise go to Login.

Any other request can also answer **426** later: show the same force-update screen.

request.description:
### What it does

Returns the app settings the apps need at start: the minimum and latest app versions per platform, whether phone verification is on, and the server time.

### Screen

**Splash** screen, on every app start (and when the app comes back after a long time in the background).

### Who can call it

Anyone, no login. It is never blocked by the app version check, so an old app can always read it.

### Request

- No body or parameters. Send the usual headers.

### Success

**200** with `data`:
- `min_supported_version`: `android` and `ios` (string or null). Below it, the app must update.
- `latest_version`: `android` and `ios` (string or null). Below it, an update is available but optional.
- `phone_verification_required` (boolean): whether sign up needs the OTP step.
- `server_time`: the server time in UTC.

**Next:** Force update, optional update dialog, then Home or Login as described in the folder.

### Errors

- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Compare versions number by number (`1.10.0` is newer than `1.9.0`). Ignore a `+build` suffix.
- A null version means "no rule": don't block or suggest anything.

item.name: 2. Sign up and login
item.description:
From a new user to a logged-in user:

1. **Sign up** screen: name, phone, password, password again, and a choice between **Customer** (`individual`) and **Business** (`business`). Submit → **Sign up**.
2. If the answer has `phone_verification_required: true`, open the **OTP** screen; otherwise go to **Login**.
3. **OTP** screen: a 6-digit code input and a **Resend code** button with a countdown that starts at `resend_available_in` seconds. Submit → **Verify phone**; resend → **Resend code** (purpose `verify_phone`), then restart the countdown at 60 seconds.
4. After the phone is verified, go to **Login** (verifying does not log in).
5. **Login** screen: phone and password → **Log in**. Save the token, then register the push token (**Push notifications**) and go to Home.
6. **Forgot password** screen: phone → **Forgot password**, then always open **Reset password**.
7. **Reset password** screen: code, new password, new password again → **Reset password**, then go to Login.

If Login answers 403 "verify your phone", open the OTP screen and call **Resend code** first.

request.description:
### What it does

Creates a new account. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**Sign up** screen, when the user taps **Create account**.

### Who can call it

Guest (not logged in).

### Request

- `name` (string, required): up to 255 characters.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.
- `account_type` (required): `individual` (customer) or `business`.
- `Accept-Language` is saved as the account language (used for SMS).

### Success

**201** with:
- `data`: the new user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).
- `phone_verification_required` (boolean): when true, an SMS code was sent.
- `resend_available_in` (number of seconds, or null): how long until **Resend code** may send another code. Null when no code was sent.
- `message`: "Your account has been created."

**Next:** If `phone_verification_required` is true, open the OTP screen with the countdown from `resend_available_in`; otherwise go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors. A phone that already has an account gets `errors.phone` = "This phone number already has an account. Please log in, or use forgot password.": show it with links to Login and Forgot password.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Register never changes an existing account. An unverified user who comes back finishes with **Resend code** and **Verify phone**, not with register again.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Confirms the phone number with the SMS code. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**OTP** screen, when the user enters the code (or taps **Verify**).

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the 6-digit code from the SMS.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your phone number has been verified.").

**Next:** Show "Phone verified" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- A code is valid for 5 minutes and allows 5 wrong tries.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sends a new SMS code for phone verification or for a password reset.

### Screen

**OTP** screen (purpose `verify_phone`) and **Reset password** screen (purpose `reset_password`), when the user taps **Resend code** after the countdown.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `purpose` (required): `verify_phone` or `reset_password`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If this phone number can receive a code, we have sent one."). Restart the resend countdown at 60 seconds.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**, and for an already verified phone: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid. Keep the **Resend** button disabled during the countdown.
- A new code replaces the old one.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Mobile login. Returns a Bearer token for this device.

### Screen

**Login** screen, when the user taps **Log in**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): up to 64 characters.
- `device_name` (string, required): up to 100 characters, for example the phone model. It names the token.

### Success

**200** with:
- `token`: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. Store it in secure storage.
- `token_type`: `Bearer`.
- `data`: the user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).

**Next:** Save `token` in secure storage, call **Save push token**, then go to Home.

### Errors

- **422:** wrong phone or password: `errors.phone` = "These credentials do not match our records." (the same for an unknown phone).
- **403:** the account is blocked, or the phone is not verified while phone verification is on. Show `message`; for "verify your phone", open the OTP screen (call **Resend code** first).
- **429:** too many login tries: 5 per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, or 20 per hour for one phone number from any IP address. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Limits: 5 tries per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, plus 20 per hour for each phone number from any IP address. Mobile and web login share these limits.

### What it does

Sends a password reset code by SMS.

### Screen

**Forgot password** screen, when the user taps **Send code**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If an account exists for this phone number, we have sent it a reset code."). Always go to the Reset password screen.

**Next:** Open the Reset password screen with the phone filled in.

### Errors

- **422:** the phone is missing or not a valid Egyptian mobile number.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Always uses the SMS code, even when phone verification is off.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sets a new password with the reset code from the SMS.

### Screen

**Reset password** screen, when the user taps **Save**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the code from the reset SMS.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been reset."). Go to Login. The user is signed out of every device, and the phone counts as verified.

**Next:** Show "Password changed" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**. Password errors come under `errors.password`.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Use the code from **Forgot password** (purpose `reset_password`); a sign-up code doesn't work here.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

item.name: 3. Account
item.description:
The logged-in user's screens:

1. **Home** and **Profile**: call **Get my account** on open (and pull to refresh). It gives the name, phone, account type, the national ID status and, for business accounts, the business profile status.
2. **Change password** screen: current password, new password, new password again → **Change password**.
3. **Settings › Log out**: first **Remove push token** (Push notifications), then **Log out**, then clear the stored token and go to Login.

request.description:
### What it does

Returns the logged-in user with everything the account screens need.

### Screen

**Home** and **Profile** screens, on open and on pull to refresh; also after the app starts with a stored token.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked (customer, business or staff).

### Request

- No body. Send the Bearer token (mobile) or the session cookie (web).

### Success

**200** with `data`, the user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).

**Next:** For business accounts, show the business profile status from `business_profile`; show the national ID status from `national_id`.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- The document `url`s expire after 5 minutes: call **me** again to refresh them.

### What it does

Changes the password of the logged-in user.

### Screen

**Change password** screen, when the user taps **Save**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `current_password` (string, required): the current password, up to 64 characters.
- `password` (string, required): the new password, 8 to 64 characters, different from the current one.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the new password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been changed."). The user stays logged in here; their other mobile logins are signed out.

**Next:** Show "Password changed" and go back. Other phones of this user are logged out.

### Errors

- **422:** `errors.current_password` (wrong current password) or `errors.password` (too short, too long, not confirmed, or the same as the current one).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- From the web, every mobile login of this user is signed out (the web session stays).

### What it does

Logs out: on mobile it deletes the current token; on the web it ends the session.

### Screen

**Settings**, when the user taps **Log out** (after **Remove push token**).

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user, blocked users too.

### Request

- No body.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("You have been logged out."). Clear the stored login and go to Login.

**Next:** Clear the stored token and go to Login.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login. (treat it as already logged out)
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Even if the call fails, clear the stored login on the device.

item.name: 4. Push notifications
item.description:
Keep the FCM push token on the server:

1. After every successful login, get the FCM token and call **Save push token** with the platform and app version.
2. When FCM gives a new token (`onTokenRefresh`), call **Save push token** again.
3. On logout, call **Remove push token** **before** **Log out**, while the login is still valid.

request.description:
### What it does

Saves the FCM push token of this device, so the user gets push notifications.

### Screen

No screen: right after login, and whenever FCM refreshes the token.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `platform` (required): `android`, `ios` or `web`.
- `push_token` (string, required): the FCM token, up to 255 characters.
- `app_version` (string, optional): up to 20 characters, for example `1.4.0`.

### Success

**201** when the token is new, **200** when it was already saved. `data`: `id`, `platform`, `app_version`, `last_seen_at`. The push token itself is never returned.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- One token belongs to one device: if it was saved for another user (someone else logged in on this phone before), it moves to the current user.

### What it does

Removes the FCM push token of this device, so it stops getting this user's notifications.

### Screen

No screen: on **Log out**, just before calling **Log out**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

### Request

- `push_token` (string, required): the same FCM token. Send it as a query parameter (or in the body).

### Success

**204** with no body. It also answers 204 when the token was not saved for this user.

### Errors

- **422:** `push_token` is missing.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Call it **before** logout: after logout the token is no longer valid.

item.name: 5. Business profile
item.description:
Business accounts only (`account_type` = `business`):

1. **Business profile** screen: on open → **Get business profile**. A 404 means there is no profile yet: show the form.
2. Show the status banner: **pending** ("waiting for review"), **approved**, or **rejected** with `rejection_reason`.

item.name: 2. Sign up and login
item.description:
From a visitor to a logged-in user:

1. On app load (and before **Log in**), call **Get CSRF cookie**.
2. **Sign up** page: name, phone, password, password again, and **Customer** or **Business** → **Sign up**.
3. If `phone_verification_required` is true, open the **OTP** page; otherwise go to **Login**.
4. **OTP** page: code input and a **Resend code** link with a countdown from `resend_available_in` → **Verify phone** / **Resend code**.
5. **Login** page: phone and password → **Log in**. Then load **Get my account** and go to the account (business accounts without a profile go to the onboarding wizard).

A 419 answer means the CSRF cookie is old: call **Get CSRF cookie** again and retry once.

### What it does

Starts a web session: the server sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` and session cookies in the browser. Not under `/api/v1`.

### Screen

When the website loads, before **Log in**, and again after a 419.

### Who can call it

Anyone (web only).

### Request

- `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`, with cookies (`credentials: 'include'` / `withCredentials: true`).
- No body.

### Success

**204** with no body. The browser now has the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. Send it back as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on the next requests (axios does this by itself).

### Errors

- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Call it again when a request answers **419**.
- In Postman, the folder script copies the cookie into `X-XSRF-TOKEN` for you.

### What it does

Creates a new account. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**Sign up** page, when the visitor clicks **Create account**.

### Who can call it

Guest (not logged in).

### Request

- `name` (string, required): up to 255 characters.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.
- `account_type` (required): `individual` (customer) or `business`.
- `Accept-Language` is saved as the account language (used for SMS).

### Success

**201** with:
- `data`: the new user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).
- `phone_verification_required` (boolean): when true, an SMS code was sent.
- `resend_available_in` (number of seconds, or null): how long until **Resend code** may send another code. Null when no code was sent.
- `message`: "Your account has been created."

**Next:** If `phone_verification_required` is true, open the OTP page with the countdown from `resend_available_in`; otherwise go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors. A phone that already has an account gets `errors.phone` = "This phone number already has an account. Please log in, or use forgot password.": show it with links to Login and Forgot password.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Register never changes an existing account. An unverified user who comes back finishes with **Resend code** and **Verify phone**, not with register again.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Confirms the phone number with the SMS code. It does not log the user in.

### Screen

**OTP** page, when the visitor submits the code.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the 6-digit code from the SMS.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your phone number has been verified.").

**Next:** Show "Phone verified" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- A code is valid for 5 minutes and allows 5 wrong tries.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sends a new SMS code for phone verification or for a password reset.

### Screen

**OTP** page (purpose `verify_phone`) and **Reset password** page (purpose `reset_password`), when the countdown is over and the visitor clicks **Resend code**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `purpose` (required): `verify_phone` or `reset_password`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If this phone number can receive a code, we have sent one."). Restart the resend countdown at 60 seconds.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**, and for an already verified phone: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid. Keep the **Resend** button disabled during the countdown.
- A new code replaces the old one.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Web login with a session cookie. No token is returned.

### Screen

**Login** page, when the visitor clicks **Log in** (after **Get CSRF cookie**).

### Who can call it

Guest, from the React website or admin panel.

### Request

- First call `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`.
- Send with cookies and the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): up to 64 characters.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the logged-in user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin). The session cookie is now set; later requests just send cookies.

**Next:** Call **Get my account**, then go to the account page (or the onboarding wizard for a business without a profile).

### Errors

- **400:** the request did not come from a trusted website domain (`SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS`), so no session could start.
- **419:** the CSRF cookie is missing or old: call `sanctum/csrf-cookie` again and retry.
- **422:** wrong phone or password: `errors.phone` = "These credentials do not match our records.".
- **403:** the account is blocked, or the phone is not verified while phone verification is on. Show `message`.
- **429:** too many login tries: 5 per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, or 20 per hour for one phone number from any IP address. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Limits: 5 tries per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, plus 20 per hour for each phone number from any IP address. Mobile and web login share these limits.

### What it does

Sends a password reset code by SMS.

### Screen

**Forgot password** page, when the visitor clicks **Send code**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("If an account exists for this phone number, we have sent it a reset code."). Always go to the Reset password screen.

**Next:** Open the Reset password page with the phone filled in.

### Errors

- **422:** the phone is missing or not a valid Egyptian mobile number.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- **Same answer for registered and unknown phones**: never tell the user whether the number has an account.
- Always uses the SMS code, even when phone verification is off.
- Within 60 seconds of the last code, nothing new is sent and the earlier code stays valid.
- Limits: 5 requests per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Sign up**, **Resend code** and **Forgot password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Sets a new password with the reset code from the SMS.

### Screen

**Reset password** page, when the visitor clicks **Save**.

### Who can call it

Guest.

### Request

- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `code` (string, required): the code from the reset SMS.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been reset."). Go to Login. The user is signed out of every device, and the phone counts as verified.

**Next:** Show "Password changed" and go to Login.

### Errors

- **422:** The same error for a wrong code, an expired code, a used code, a code with too many wrong tries (5 per code) and an unknown phone: `errors.code` = "The code is wrong or has expired…". Show it under the code input and offer **Resend code**. Password errors come under `errors.password`.
- **429:** too many attempts from this phone number or this IP address (users on the same network share the IP limit). Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Use the code from **Forgot password** (purpose `reset_password`); a sign-up code doesn't work here.
- Limits: 5 tries per phone number and 20 per IP address every 60 minutes (users on the same network share the IP limit). **Verify phone** and **Reset password** share one limit per phone.

### What it does

Returns the logged-in user with everything the account screens need.

### Screen

**Account menu** on every page load, and the **Account** page.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked (customer, business or staff).

### Request

request.description:
### What it does

Starts a web session: the server sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` and session cookies in the browser. Not under `/api/v1`.

### Screen

When the admin panel loads, before **Log in**, and again after a 419.

### Who can call it

Anyone (web only).

### Request

- `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`, with cookies (`credentials: 'include'` / `withCredentials: true`).
- No body.

### Success

**204** with no body. The browser now has the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie. Send it back as the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header on the next requests (axios does this by itself).

### Errors

- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Call it again when a request answers **419**.
- In Postman, the folder script copies the cookie into `X-XSRF-TOKEN` for you.

### What it does

Web login with a session cookie. No token is returned.

### Screen

**Admin login** page, when the staff member clicks **Log in**.

### Who can call it

Guest, from the React website or admin panel.

### Request

- First call `GET {{appUrl}}/sanctum/csrf-cookie`.
- Send with cookies and the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`.
- `password` (string, required): up to 64 characters.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the logged-in user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin). The session cookie is now set; later requests just send cookies.

**Next:** Call **Get my account** and build the menu from `permissions`.

### Errors

- **400:** the request did not come from a trusted website domain (`SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS`), so no session could start.
- **419:** the CSRF cookie is missing or old: call `sanctum/csrf-cookie` again and retry.
- **422:** wrong phone or password: `errors.phone` = "These credentials do not match our records.".
- **403:** the account is blocked, or the phone is not verified while phone verification is on. Show `message`.
- **429:** too many login tries: 5 per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, or 20 per hour for one phone number from any IP address. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then let the user retry.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Limits: 5 tries per minute for each phone number from the same IP address, plus 20 per hour for each phone number from any IP address. Mobile and web login share these limits.

### Who can call it

Staff with `national_ids.review` (ops, admin, super admin).

- Path `user`: the user `id`.
- `reason` (string, required): up to 255 characters, written for the client.

### Success

**200** with the review item (`status` = `rejected`, `rejection_reason`). Close the dialog and remove it from the list.

### Errors

item.name: 4. Users
item.description:
Customer and business accounts. Needs `users.view` to see, `users.block` to block and unblock:

1. **Users** page: a search box (name or phone) and filters for account type, status, phone verified, national ID status and business profile status → **List users**, paged, newest first.
2. Clicking a row opens the **User details** page → **Get user**: account data, the national ID images and the business profile with its links and documents.

request.description:
### What it does

Lists customer and business accounts (never staff), newest first, with search and filters.

### Screen

**Users** page, on open, on search, on filter change and on page change.

### Who can call it

Staff with `users.view` (support, ops, admin, super admin).

### Request

- Query `search` (optional, up to 100 characters), Arabic digits are fine:
  - a full Egyptian mobile number in any format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`) finds that exact phone;
  - 4 or more digits find phones that contain them (a leading 0 is ignored, so `0100000` finds `+20100000…`);
  - anything else searches the name.
- Query `account_type` (optional): `individual` or `business`.
- Query `status` (optional): `active` or `blocked`.
- Query `phone_verified` (optional): `true` or `false`.
- Query `national_id_status` (optional): `none` (never uploaded), `pending`, `approved` or `rejected`.
- Query `business_profile_status` (optional): `pending`, `approved` or `rejected` (only business accounts with a profile).
- Query `per_page` (optional, 1 to 100, default 20) and `page`.

### Success

**200** with `data`: a list of users, each with `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale`, `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `reviewed_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `created_at`. In the list, `business_profile` has the profile data without `business_type`, `links` and `documents`; open the user for those. Plus `meta` and `links` for pages.

### Errors

- **422:** an unknown filter value or `per_page` out of range.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Keep the search and filters in the page URL, so the list survives a reload.

### What it does

Returns one customer or business account for the User details page: the national ID and the business profile with links and documents.

### Screen

**User details** page, on open.

### Who can call it

Staff with `users.view`.

### Request

- Path `customer`: the user `id` (from the list). No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale`, `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `reviewed_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `created_at`, with `business_profile` in full: `id`, `business_type` (`id`, `name`), `business_name`, `description`, `avg_daily_orders`, `tax_registration_number`, `verification_status` (`pending` | `approved` | `rejected`), `rejection_reason`, `reviewed_at`, `links` (`id`, `type`, `url`), `documents` (`national_id_front`, `national_id_back`, `tax_register` (the commercial register, السجل التجاري), `tax_card` (the tax card, البطاقة الضريبية): each a file with `file_name`, `mime_type`, `size`, `uploaded_at` and a signed `url`, or null), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

### Errors

- **404:** no customer with this id (staff accounts are 404 here too: manage them under **Staff**).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- A file comes without `url` when the staff member can't view that kind of document (`national_ids.view` for the national ID, `business_profiles.view` for business documents).
- The `url`s expire after 5 minutes: call it again to refresh them.

### What it does

### Screen

**User details** page, when the staff member confirms the **Block** dialog with a reason.

### Who can call it

- Path `customer`: the user `id`.
- `reason` (string, required): up to 255 characters, for the staff (the user only sees "Your account has been blocked").

### Success

**200** with `data`, the user (`status` = `blocked`, `blocked_reason`): `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale`, `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `reviewed_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `created_at`.

**Next:** Show the blocked banner with the reason and the **Unblock** button.

### Errors

- **404:** no customer with this id (staff accounts are 404 here too: manage them under **Staff**).
- **422:** `errors.reason` (missing or too long).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Blocking a blocked user answers 200 and only replaces the reason.

### What it does

Unblocks a customer or business account and clears the reason.

### Screen

**User details** page, when the staff member clicks **Unblock** (confirm first).

### Who can call it

Staff with `users.block` (ops, admin, super admin).

### Request

- Path `customer`: the user `id`. No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the user (`status` = `active`, `blocked_reason` = null): `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale`, `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `reviewed_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `created_at`.

### Errors

- **404:** no customer with this id (staff accounts are 404 here too: manage them under **Staff**).

- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.

item.name: 5. Business types
item.description:
The business types customers pick from. Needs `business_types.view` to see, `business_types.manage` to change:

1. **Business types** page with tabs **Active** and **Inactive** → **List business types** with `is_active`, an optional `search`, paged, in sort order.

request.description:
### What it does

Lists every business type, active and inactive, in sort order.

### Screen

**Business types** page, on open, on tab change (`is_active`), on search and on page change.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.view` (support, ops, admin, super admin).

**200** with `data`: a list of business types, each with `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`. Plus `meta` and `links` for pages.

### Errors

- **422:** an invalid `is_active`, `search` too long or `per_page` out of range.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Show **Delete** only when `business_profiles_count` is 0; otherwise offer **Deactivate**.

### What it does

Returns one business type with its name in both languages, to fill the edit form.

### Screen

**Edit business type** form, on open.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.view`.

### Request

- Path `businessType`: the type `id`. No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`: `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

### Errors

- **404:** no business type with this id.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.

### What it does

Creates a business type.

### Screen

**Add business type** form, when the staff member clicks **Save**.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.manage` (admin, super admin).

### Request

- `name.ar` and `name.en` (strings, both required): up to 100 characters each, as `{ "name": { "ar": "مطعم", "en": "Restaurant" } }`.
- `is_active` (boolean, optional): default `true`.
- `sort_order` (number, optional): 0 to 65535. Left out, the type goes to the end of the list.

### Success

**201** with `data`, the new type: `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

**Next:** Close the form and reload the list.

### Errors

- **422:** field errors. A name another type already uses (ignoring letter case) gets `errors["name.ar"]` or `errors["name.en"]` = "Another business type already has this name."
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- An active type shows up in the public **Get business types** list at once.

### What it does

Updates a business type. Send only the fields that change.

### Screen

**Edit business type** form, when the staff member clicks **Save**.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.manage` (admin, super admin).

### Request

- Path `businessType`: the type `id`.
- Any of `name` (both `ar` and `en` when sent), `is_active`, `sort_order` (same rules as create).

### Success

**200** with `data`, the updated type: `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

**Next:** Close the form and update the row.

### Errors

- **404:** no business type with this id.
- **422:** field errors, for example a name with one language only, or a name another type already uses (ignoring letter case).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Renaming a type changes the name every business profile with this type shows.

Activates a business type, so it shows in the public list again.

**Business types** page (Inactive tab), when the staff member clicks **Activate** on a row.

Staff with `business_types.manage` (admin, super admin).

- Path `businessType`: the type `id`. No body.

**200** with `data`, the type (`is_active` = true): `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`. Move it to the Active tab.

### Errors

- **404:** no business type with this id.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Activating an active type also answers 200.

### What it does

Deactivates a business type: it leaves the public list, and new business profiles can't pick it.

### Screen

**Business types** page (Active tab), when the staff member clicks **Deactivate** on a row, or **Deactivate** in the delete dialog.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.manage` (admin, super admin).

### Request

- Path `businessType`: the type `id`. No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the type (`is_active` = false): `id`, `name` (`ar` and `en`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, `business_profiles_count` (how many business profiles use it), `created_at`, `updated_at`. Move it to the Inactive tab.

### Errors

- **404:** no business type with this id.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Existing business profiles keep the type. Use this instead of delete for a type that is in use.

### What it does

Deletes a business type that no business profile uses.

### Screen

**Business types** page, when the staff member confirms the **Delete** dialog.

### Who can call it

Staff with `business_types.manage` (admin, super admin).

### Request

- Path `businessType`: the type `id`. No body.

### Success

**204** with no body. Remove the row.

**Next:** Remove the row. On 422, keep the dialog open with the message and a **Deactivate** button.

### Errors

- **404:** no business type with this id.
- **422:** a business profile uses the type: `errors.business_type` = "This business type is used by business profiles, so it cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead." Show it in the dialog with a **Deactivate** button.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

- Ask for confirmation first; a delete can't be undone.

item.name: 6. Staff
item.description:
Admin panel accounts. Super admins only (`staff.manage`): hide this menu item for everyone else.

request.description:
### What it does

Lists staff members with their role and status, newest first.

### Screen

**Staff** page, on open and on page change.

### Who can call it

Staff with `staff.manage` (super admin only).

### Request

- Query `per_page` (optional, 1 to 100, default 20) and `page`.

### Success

**200** with `data`: a list of staff members, each with `id`, `name`, `phone`, `role` (`super_admin` | `admin` | `ops` | `support`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `created_at`. Plus `meta` and `links` for pages.

### Errors

- **422:** `per_page` out of range.
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Hide the **Staff** menu item for users without `staff.manage`.

### What it does

Creates a staff account with a role. The staff member can log in to the admin panel at once with this phone and password.

### Screen

**Add staff** form, when the super admin clicks **Save**.

### Who can call it

Staff with `staff.manage` (super admin only).

### Request

- `name` (string, required): up to 255 characters.
- `phone` (string, required): any Egyptian mobile format (`01000000000`, `+201000000000`, `00201000000000`, spaces, dashes and Arabic digits are fine). The server saves it as `+201XXXXXXXXX`. It must not belong to any account, customer or staff.
- `password` (string, required): 8 to 64 characters.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the same password again.
- `role` (required): `admin`, `ops` or `support`. `super_admin` can't be given through the API.

### Success

**201** with `data`, the new staff member: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `role` (`super_admin` | `admin` | `ops` | `support`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `created_at`.

**Next:** Close the form and reload the list.

- **422:** field errors. A phone that already has an account gets `errors.phone` = "This phone number already belongs to an account."
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- The phone counts as verified. Share the password with the staff member privately and ask them to change it after the first login.

Changes a staff member's role.

### Screen

**Staff** page, when the super admin picks a new role for a row and confirms.

Staff with `staff.manage` (super admin only).

- Path `staff`: the staff member `id`.
- `role` (required): `admin`, `ops` or `support`.

**200** with `data`, the staff member with the new role: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `role` (`super_admin` | `admin` | `ops` | `support`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `created_at`.

- **422:** `errors.role` (unknown or `super_admin`), or `errors.staff`: "You cannot change your own role." or "This is the last active super admin, so it cannot be blocked or demoted."
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

- Hide the change-role action on the logged-in user's own row. The new permissions apply from their next request.

### What it does

Blocks a staff member with a reason. Their logins stop working at once.

### Screen

**Staff** page, when the super admin confirms the **Block** dialog with a reason.

Staff with `staff.manage` (super admin only).

- Path `staff`: the staff member `id`.
- `reason` (string, required): up to 255 characters.

### Success

- **422:** `errors.reason` (missing or too long), or `errors.staff`: "You cannot block your own account." or "This is the last active super admin, so it cannot be blocked or demoted."
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** not a staff account, blocked, or missing the permission (`message` says which). Hide this action for users without the permission.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Hide the block action on the logged-in user's own row. Blocking a blocked staff member answers 200 and only replaces the reason.

### What it does

Unblocks a staff member and clears the reason.

### Screen

**Staff** page, when the super admin clicks **Unblock** on a blocked row (confirm first).

### Who can call it

Staff with `staff.manage` (super admin only).

### Request

- Path `staff`: the staff member `id`. No body.

### Success

**200** with `data`, the staff member (`status` = `active`): `id`, `name`, `phone`, `role` (`super_admin` | `admin` | `ops` | `support`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `blocked_reason`, `created_at`.

request.description:
### What it does

Returns the logged-in user with everything the account screens need.

### Screen

Every panel load, to show the user in the top bar and build the menu.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked (customer, business or staff).

### Request

- No body. Send the Bearer token (mobile) or the session cookie (web).

### Success

**200** with `data`, the user: `id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `account_type` (`individual` | `business`), `locale` (`ar` | `en`), `status` (`active` | `blocked`), `is_phone_verified`, `phone_verified_at`, `national_id` (`status`: null | `pending` | `approved` | `rejected`, `rejection_reason`, `verified_at`, `front` and `back` files with a signed `url`), `business_profile` (or null), `roles` (staff role names, for display only; an empty list for customers) and `permissions` (what the user may do; an empty list for customers, every permission for a super admin).

**Next:** Show or hide menu items and buttons from `permissions`.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- The document `url`s expire after 5 minutes: call **me** again to refresh them.

### What it does

Changes the password of the logged-in user.

### Screen

**Change password** page, when the staff member clicks **Save**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user who is not blocked.

- `current_password` (string, required): the current password, up to 64 characters.
- `password` (string, required): the new password, 8 to 64 characters, different from the current one.
- `password_confirmation` (string, required): the new password again.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("Your password has been changed."). The user stays logged in here; their other mobile logins are signed out.

### Errors

- **422:** `errors.current_password` (wrong current password) or `errors.password` (too short, too long, not confirmed, or the same as the current one).
- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login.
- **403:** the account is blocked (`message` says so). Show the message and log the user out.
- **426 (mobile):** the app is too old. Show the force-update screen.
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- From the web, every mobile login of this user is signed out (the web session stays).

### What it does

Logs out: on mobile it deletes the current token; on the web it ends the session.

### Screen

**Top bar › Log out**.

### Who can call it

Any logged-in user, blocked users too.

### Request

- No body.

### Success

**200** with `message` ("You have been logged out."). Clear the stored login and go to Login.

**Next:** Show the login page.

### Errors

- **401:** not logged in, or the login expired. Clear the stored login and go to Login. (treat it as already logged out)
- **500:** show a generic error and a retry button.

### Notes

- Even if the call fails, clear the stored login on the device.
